name: Inrotech-Crawler
summary: Mobile welding robot that runs on flexible titanium rails magnetically attached to large steel structures and does adaptive multipass welds in any position; for pipes, tanks, ship hulls, bridges and other big structures in workshops or on construction sites.

germany.statusNote: Danish (EU) maker, now with Lincoln Electric branding on its site, sells on request (brochure and robot demo requests). No German dealer or public price found; a German customer case (Liebherr-Rostock) is listed.

sellers.name: Inrotech A/S
sellers.note: C. F. Tietgens Boulevard 26, 5220 Odense SØ, Denmark. Brochure and demo requests on the product page.

specs.label: Track
specs.value: flexible titanium rails attached by magnets
specs.conditions: flat, curved, vertical or overhead surfaces
specs.quote: The Inrotech-Crawler® travels on flexible titanium rails, magnetically attaching to large steel structures—flat, curved, vertical, overhead

specs.label: Smallest surface radius
specs.quote: The Inrotech-Crawler can be positioned on flat or curved surfaces (down to 1 m. radius).

specs.label: Welding positions
specs.value: PA (1G), PC (2G), PE overhead (4G), PF vertical up (3G, 3F, 5G)

specs.label: Weld planning
specs.value: line scanner finds the groove and calculates passes, positions, speed and weaving
specs.quote: The robot now automatically identifies the welding groove by means of a line scanner and automatically calculates the number of passes, location of each pass, welding speed and weaving pattern

notes: Rail-mounted carriage with a welding torch, moved to the workpiece; the operator sets start and stop points and presses start.
No programming and no CAD transfer needed (maker).

images.alt: Inrotech-Crawler welding robot on its rail

evidence.task: Adaptive multipass butt welds on large pipes, ship blocks, storage tanks and construction steelwork, in workshops or on construction sites (maker)
evidence.note: Customer case named on the page: Liebherr-Rostock GmbH (details not read).
